question: Will Donald Trump's approval rating reach a new low in the second half of October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin approve average has set repeated new lows (Sept 23-24 at 37.4-37.6%, Sept 28, net -23.5 on Oct 3-5), then bounced to net -21.9 on Oct 8 on a friendly TIPP poll. The record approve is likely ~37.0-37.4%; current approve is about 0.4-0.8 points above it. A 17-day window (Oct 15-31) with downward drift and normal swings in the average gives a meaningful chance of a new low. Pulling the other way: possible pre-midterm consolidation or a rally, and the long June-Aug stretch when the May low held. No matching market: Polymarket's year-end 'how low' market (same source) is a near-miss, thin and possibly resolved.

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin approve average set repeated term lows Sep–early Oct 2026, with the latest ~37.1% (net -23.5) around Oct 3-5. By Oct 8 it had bounced to net -21.9 (approve ~37.6-37.9), mostly on one TIPP poll whose weight will fade. A strictly lower value is needed during Oct 15-31 (17 days), i.e. a ~0.4-0.8pt drop from the current level, or a further low by Oct 14 followed by another in the window. The persistent downward drift and frequent recent lows favor Yes; mean reversion, a possible pre-midterm partisan rally and the precedent of the May low holding all summer favor No. Net: about a coin flip, slightly below.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the instrument (CSV 'approve' daily average), the window (Oct 15-31), a record approve around 37.0-37.4 set late Sep to Oct 5, and current approve ~37.5-37.9. Run 3's Wikipedia table value (37.1 approve near Oct 1, net -23.5) is consistent with Runs 1-2's inferred ranges, so I adopt ~37.1 as the bar, with ±0.2 uncertainty I could not settle offline. The rest of the spread (0.45-0.50) is a judgment about drift vs a pre-midterm rebound; no evidence breaks the tie. The persistent declining trend and the fading one-poll bounce roughly offset the mean reversion seen after past lows (the May low held for ~4 months). I land at 0.47. No matching human market exists; the Polymarket year-end market is a near-miss and is used only as weak evidence of expected further decline.
